title: Double `+ - * /` are binary64, round to nearest even, on macOS arm64 (D31)
verdict: binary64, round to nearest even, no contraction, no flush to zero: native for D31
description: On macOS arm64, C++ `double` operators, one vectorized kernel per operator: every result of `+ - * /` on doubles is the exact result rounded once to binary64, to nearest with ties to even, bit for bit, on 22432 operations (22432 per path).

The operands: every pair of a table of edge values (zeros, subnormals, the smallest normal, one and its neighbour, `2⁻⁵³`, `2⁵³`, the largest double, the infinities, NaN, and their negatives), pseudo-random operands at every exponent from 0 to 2046 paired with operands at random exponents, both ways round, and ties (`1 + 2⁻⁵³`, `1 + 3 · 2⁻⁵³`, subnormals times `0.5`).

No contraction: `a * b - c`, with `c` the rounded product of 2,000 random pairs whose product is inexact, is `0.0` for every pair; a fused multiply-add would give the residual. No flush to zero: every subnormal result is the subnormal.

Signed zeros and NaN agree with IEEE 754 on two columns; a NaN's sign is not compared (D31 leaves it open; polars-exec-platform records it per platform). Division by zero is left out: it is `on_division_by_zero` (the engine's `fp.div` facts).
No upstream test pins the platform's rounding; the probe is rerun per platform and engine version.
reference: D31: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply` and `divide` of doubles are the exact result rounded once to binary64, to nearest, ties to even (`FloatCode.fadd` … in `core/Sverify/Core/FloatArith.lean`). The engine is native for D31 on this platform.
